items.title: Attackers Exploit Zero-Day in End-of-Life D-Link Routers
items.description: Hackers are attacking a critical zero-day flaw in unsupported D-Link DSL routers to run arbitrary commands.

items.title: Critical jsPDF flaw lets hackers steal secrets via generated PDFs
items.description: The jsPDF library for generating PDF documents in JavaScript applications is vulnerable to a critical vulnerability that allows an attacker to steal sensitive data from the local filesystem by including it in generated files. [...]

items.title: Phishers Exploit Office 365 Users Who Let Their Guard Down
items.description: Microsoft said that Office 365 tenants with weak configurations and who don't have strict anti-spoofing protection enabled are especially vulnerable.

items.title: ChatGPT is losing market share as Google Gemini gains ground
items.description: New data suggests that ChatGPT is losing its market share to Gemini on the web. It's unclear if Gemini is also gaining ground in the mobile space. [...]

items.title: Logitech Options+, G HUB macOS apps break after certificate expires
items.description: Logitech's Options+ and G Hub apps on macOS stopped working after their code-signing certificate expired, leaving users unable to launch them on Apple systems. [...]

items.title: Hackers Using Malicious Imageless QR Codes to Render Phishing Attack Via HTML Table
items.description: A recent phishing campaign is abusing QR codes in a new way, turning simple HTML tables into working codes that redirect users to malicious sites. Instead of embedding a QR image in the email body, the attackers build the code from hundreds of tiny table cells, each styled as black or white. items.title: Max severity Ni8mare flaw lets hackers hijack n8n servers
items.description: A maximum severity vulnerability dubbed "Ni8mare" allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to take control over locally deployed instances of the N8N workflow automation platform. [...]

items.title: Black Cat Behind SEO Poisoning Malware Campaign Targeting Popular Software Searches
items.description: A cybercrime gang known as Black Cat has been attributed to a search engine optimization (SEO) poisoning campaign that employs fraudulent sites advertising popular software to trick users into downloading a backdoor capable of stealing sensitive data.
